nodes.question: How does the analysis track research alignment with policy objectives?
nodes.answer: The analysis traces the heterogeneity in past research and tracks whether currently funded projects are aligned with policy objectives.
nodes.paragraph: Methods include both quantitative bibliometric databases and qualitative thematic analysis (Xiao & Watson, 2019) using review protocols such as PICO(S), SPIDER, SPAR-4- SLR, PRISMA, and TOPIC+M (Methley et al., 2014; Mohamed Shaffril et al., 2021; Moher et al., 2009; Page et al., 2021). We refer to Mishra et al. (2024) and Ciarli et al. (2022) for such an SLR on SDGs and to Ralph and Arora (2024) for SDG 8 in particular. These approaches analyse finalized research output and, therefore, can be expected to be biased towards positive findings (Scheel et al., 2021). Moreover, given the lengthy peer review process and publication delays, SLRs may fail to provide a timely overview of the current research agenda. We propose an alternative approach that monitors the intended ex-ante research efforts in funded research projects, providing a complementary view of research activity to a standard SLR. The analysis traces the heterogeneity in past research and tracks whether currently funded projects are aligned with policy objectives.

nodes.question: What distinction do most studies make regarding the focus of policy integration?
nodes.answer: Most studies focus on the system level interacting effects of policy integration rather than the operational level.

Likewise, when implementing policies, actors can plan their activities over one speci C problem or over multiple societal challenges (Lyles et al. 2018 ). While most studies tend to focus on the system level interacting effects(e.g. Duguma et al., 2014 ; Berry et al. 2015 ), and speci - cally address policy integration (Di Gregorio et al. 2017 ; Cejudo & Trein 2023 ; Biesbroek, Candel 2020 ), this research focuses on the operational level of integration, where solutions have a physical impact. Notwithstanding these bene its, researchers also admit that integration can imply high transaction costs and may have unintended side effects due to the impossibility of predicting the risks in such a complex multi-sector setting (Bryson et al. 2006 ; M rker et al. 2018 ; Kongsager 2018 ; Metz et al. 2020 ). In addition, De Lo and Patterson ( 2017 p. 93) state that challenges for which causes, effects, and interests are relatively clear, uncontentious, and bound by sector are generally tackled most ef ciently using a sectoral scope.

nodes.question: How has the Federal Government of Australia aligned its policy direction concerning the wellbeing economy?
nodes.answer: The Federal Government of Australia has moved its policy direction to align with wellbeing economy principles through the announcement of a wellbeing budget.
nodes.paragraph: Governments who are part of the WEAII acknowledge the role of economic growth and wealth creation as one potential indicator of collective wellbe - ing. However, they also acknowledge the importance of several other key principles which form the foundations of a wellbeing economy. These include: dignity everyone has enough to ensure that they can live in comfort, safety and happiness; nature and climate a restored and safe natural world for all life; social connection sense of belonging and institutions that serve the common good; fairness justice in all its dimensions is at the heart of economic systems and the gap between the richest and poorest in society is reduced and participation citizens are actively encouraged to engage in their communities and local economies [1 ]. The Federal Government of Australia has recently moved policy direction to align itself with the principles of a well- being economy through the announcement of a wellbe- ing budget [7 , 8]. Australia S first wellbeing budget was delivered in October 2022; it not only projected traditional measures of employment, gross domestic product (GDP) and national debt but also included measures of health and education outcomes, environmental sustainability, social inclusion and inequality for the first time [9 ].

nodes.question: How can visual mapping of policies across the life cycle help in understanding the interconnections between policies according to CE strategies and product life cycle stages?
nodes.answer: Visual mapping can aid in understanding the interconnections between policies by revealing points of harmony or contention across the life cycle, thus assisting in strategic decision-making and policy alignment.
